sentences.text: Wilden narrates that magic once existed but faded as technology advanced.
He expresses hope that a little magic remains in his sons.
Laurel wakes Ian for his birthday while a pet dragon jumps on him.
Ian talks with his mother about his birthday and avoiding driving practice.
Barley confronts Ian for touching his game board, and Laurel intervenes playfully.
Officer Bronco tries to get Barley to stop protecting an old fountain from demolition.
At home Laurel urges Barley to think about his future instead of the past.
Barley tries to get Ian to play his board game and don his father's sweatshirt.
Ian recalls only three memories of his late father before rushing off to school.
A stranger recognizes Wilden's old college sweatshirt and shares fond memories of him with Ian.
Ian negotiates with a classmate about foot placement in class.
During a driving test Ian panics and cannot merge into traffic, forcing the instructor to pull over.
Ian awkwardly tries to invite classmates to his birthday party.
Barley arrives loudly in his van Guinevere, embarrassing Ian in front of the classmates.
Ian cancels the party out of embarrassment and leaves.
Barley promises a birthday ceremony later while driving Ian home.
They arrive home and call for their mother, who is absent.
An old cassette recording of young Laurel and Wilden plays, later intercut with Ian pretending to talk to his father.
Barley and Laurel banter over Barley's role-play antics and his gap year.
Ian asks Laurel what his father was like, and she shares that he once lacked confidence too.
Laurel gives the brothers a gift from their late father.
The boys discover a wizard staff, a Phoenix Gem, and a letter describing a visitation spell to resurrect their father for one day.
Barley reads the incantation aloud, causing a strange reaction from the staff.
Laurel comforts the boys, unaware of what has begun, then leaves for cake.
Ian casts the visitation spell alone but is interrupted by Barley mid-incantation.
Only the lower half of Wilden's body reforms as the gem disintegrates.
The brothers realize the spell only lasts until sunset the next day.
Barley proposes finding another Phoenix Gem at the Manticore's Tavern to finish the spell.
The brothers set off in Guinevere with Wilden's legs, Ian practicing magic along the way.
Laurel discovers the boys and Wilden are missing after finding cake and Blazey underfoot.
In the van, Ian struggles to cast a levitation spell despite Barley's coaching about heart's fire.
The brothers arrive at the once-legendary tavern, now a family restaurant.
They mistake a costumed employee for the real Manticore before finding Corey overwhelmed with orders.
Corey offers only a children's menu as a joke, but Barley recognizes it as the real map.
Ian pleads with Corey for the map, revealing their quest to meet their resurrected father.
Confronted about her mundane life, Corey furiously reverts to her fearsome Manticore form and drives out customers.
In her rage she accidentally sets the tavern and map on fire.
Ian uses a new levitation spell to save Barley from a falling beam as they escape the fire.
They celebrate that the spell worked despite losing the real map.
Using the children's menu clue, the brothers determine the gem is at Raven's Point in the mountains.
Barley insists on taking the perilous Path of Peril instead of the expressway, but Ian argues for the faster route.
Laurel calls Colt worried about the boys, then sees the tavern fire and rushes off.
Laurel meets Corey the Manticore, who warns her of a curse the boys may awaken.
Barley shows Wilden the van's rebuilt parts while Ian keeps his growing list of father activities.
Realizing they won't finish everything, Barley jokes about their mother's boyfriend.
The van runs low on fuel, so Ian attempts a growth spell on the gas can under Barley's distracting coaching.
The spell misfires and shrinks Ian instead of enlarging the can, causing an argument between the brothers.
Tiny Ian and Barley walk to a gas station where Ian is nearly stepped on and mocked by strangers.
Meanwhile Corey flies Laurel to help, explaining the Guardian Curse and the sword needed to defeat it.
Barley provokes a sprite biker gang, Dewdrop, by criticizing their ancestors' loss of flight.
The furious sprites chase the brothers as they flee in Guinevere.
The sprite gang pursues the van on bikes while Ian is forced to merge and drive under pressure.
They escape the sprites and Wilden's spell effects visibly begin fading.
Police pull the van over; Ian disguises himself as Officer Bronco to protect their secret.
Ian must answer only truthfully and inadvertently reveals Gore's low opinion of Barley as a screwup.
The disguise fades and Barley is hurt on overhearing officers call him a screwup.
Barley angrily confronts Ian about being blamed and the two argue over decisions and trust.
Wilden dances comically to the car radio, easing the tension between the brothers.
Ian agrees to try Barley's suggested Path of Peril route.
Laurel and Corey confront pawnbroker Grecklin to buy back the enchanted Curse Crusher sword.
Grecklin raises the price absurdly once he realizes the sword's value, and the women forcibly take it, injuring the shopkeeper.
Colt calls Laurel worried, but she rushes off with Corey to find the boys.
The brothers sing about their quest and enter the treacherous Path of Peril with Wilden.
Barley warns of dangerous creatures that could be lurking on the undeveloped path.
Officer Bronco catches up and orders the boys home, but Ian unexpectedly drives away.
This triggers a police chase as Gore radios for backup.
Barley has Ian cast a lightning spell to trigger a landslide, sacrificing Guinevere to block the pursuers.
Barley mourns the loss of his beloved van.
The brothers continue on foot through a storm toward Raven's Point.
They encounter unicorns and find raven statues leading down into a cave system.
Ian magically enlarges an object to float on and casts a velocity spell to speed them through the tunnel.
Meanwhile Laurel and Corey, joined by sprites after crashing, take to the skies to catch up.
Barley confesses he was too afraid to say goodbye to their dying father.
The brothers reach a final gauntlet of traps guarding the Phoenix Gem.
They narrowly escape a gelatinous cube and a triggered trap by using shields and jumping.
They hold their breath through flooded passage and emerge believing they found the gem's location.
The party emerges from the cave only to find themselves back at Ian's high school.
Realizing the gem is actually in the mountain they left behind, Ian lashes out and calls Barley a screwup before storming off.
Barley searches a fountain for the gem and is forcibly removed by construction workers who think him a nuisance.
Flashback clips of earlier encouragement between the brothers replay as Ian reflects.
Ian reviews his list of father activities and realizes Barley has been like a father to him.
Barley discovers the gem in the fountain and retrieves it, unknowingly triggering the curse.
Debris combines into a dragon-shaped golem that attacks, forcing people to flee.
Barley apologizes to Ian as the sun nears setting, and Ian recasts the visitation spell.
Corey arrives flying with Laurel, who drives the magic sword into the dragon's heart.
As Wilden's upper body regenerates, Barley volunteers to distract the dragon so Ian can meet their father.
Instead Ian sends Barley ahead to say goodbye, acknowledging his role as a father figure.
With Laurel's help Ian fights off and destroys the dragon.
Wilden dissipates after the reunion, and Barley tells Ian their father is proud of him as they share a hug.
Ian's confidence and spellcasting have visibly improved as he tells his story to schoolmates.
Barley greets his mother and Colt warmly before heading off on patrol.
The brothers set off together on a new quest in a new van.
A song plays over the closing credits.

sentences.text: A narrated legend describes a legendary warrior fighting many foes.
Po is woken from a dream and told he is late for work.
Po mimics the Furious Five with action figures before rushing downstairs.
Po's father Mr. Ping questions him about his dream and pushes him toward the noodle business.
The Furious Five train under Shifu, who criticizes their performance.
Oogway tells Shifu he has had a vision that Tai Lung will return.
Shifu orders extra security at the prison and Oogway says it is time for the Dragon Warrior selection.
Word spreads that the Dragon Warrior will be chosen, and Po rushes to sell noodles at the event.
Po tries to reach the tournament but is repeatedly turned away and locked out.
Oogway declares the historic day has come as the Furious Five perform before the crowd.
Po launches himself into the arena using fireworks and lands in front of the crowd.
Oogway unexpectedly points to Po as the Dragon Warrior, shocking everyone including Shifu.
Zeng delivers Shifu's warning to the guards at Tai Lung's prison.
The guards taunt the chained Tai Lung, who reacts with menace.
Po wanders the Hall of Warriors in awe, accidentally breaking an artifact.
Shifu confronts Po, insulting his body and doubting he can master kung fu.
Shifu nearly uses the Wuxi Finger Hold on Po before warning him he will make him regret being chosen.
Po attempts training exercises and is repeatedly hurt by the equipment and the Five.
The Five mock Po afterward, doubting Oogway's choice.
Po tries to bond with Crane at night but is told he doesn't belong there.
Tigress tells Po he is a disgrace and should leave by morning.
Po eats peaches with Oogway and admits he feels he can never measure up to the Five.
Oogway encourages Po with the idea that today is a gift.
An alarm sounds as Tai Lung breaks free of his chains and fights through the guards.
Tai Lung defeats the guards and escapes, telling Zeng to warn the palace he is coming.
Shifu finds Po has quit, stuck in a training device.
Shifu trains Po harshly with the Furious Five's obstacle courses, causing him pain.
Mantis attempts acupuncture on Po while others joke about his weight.
The Five tell Po the story of how Shifu raised Tai Lung as his son and trained him.
Oogway rejected Tai Lung for the Dragon Scroll, sensing darkness, and Tai Lung rampaged until Shifu stopped him.
Tigress scolds Po for treating his role as a joke, and Mantis accidentally injures Shifu.
Oogway tells Shifu to let go of control and believe in Po as his destiny.
Oogway makes Shifu promise to believe, then dissolves into blossoms as he departs.
Po shares a meal and jokes with the Five, who now warm to him.
Shifu catches them joking and announces Tai Lung has escaped and only Po can stop him.
Terrified, Po tries to flee but Shifu blocks him.
Po confronts Shifu, revealing he stayed despite being mistreated, hoping to be changed.
Shifu admits he doesn't know how to make Po the Dragon Warrior.
The Five decide to accompany Po to face Tai Lung rather than stop him.
The group travels while Po sneaks a snack, caught by Shifu.
Shifu notices Po has done a perfect split by accident while reaching for a cookie.
Shifu brings Po to the birthplace of kung fu and agrees to train him with food as motivation.
Po trains rapidly, mastering feats when chasing dumplings, and duels Shifu with new skill.
Tai Lung fights the Furious Five along the road, overpowering them one by one.
Tigress and the others fall to Tai Lung's paralyzing nerve attack.
Shifu tells the wounded Po that he can defeat Tai Lung and believes he is ready.
Shifu presents Po the Dragon Scroll, but when opened it proves blank.
Believing himself a fraud, Po is sent to evacuate villagers while Shifu stays to face Tai Lung alone.
Po reunites with his father, who reveals the Secret Ingredient Soup has no secret ingredient.
Mr. Ping says belief is what makes something special.
Thunder rumbles as Tai Lung arrives at the Jade Palace to confront Shifu.
Tai Lung accuses Shifu of denying him his destiny and the two fight brutally.
Shifu apologizes for his pride, but is defeated; Tai Lung demands the scroll.
Po arrives declaring himself the Dragon Warrior and fights Tai Lung amid falling debris.
Tai Lung wrests the scroll from Po and reads it, but finds it blank like before.
Po explains the scroll's message that there is no secret ingredient, just belief in oneself.
Enraged, Tai Lung nerve-strikes Po, who is unaffected due to his body fat.
Po overpowers Tai Lung and uses the self-taught Wuxi Finger Hold to vanquish him.
Po returns to a celebrating crowd and is hailed as the Dragon Warrior by his father.
Po finds Shifu injured but alive, who names him the Dragon Warrior who brought peace.
Po and Shifu go to eat together as a closing song plays over the credits.

sentences.text: Eep narrates that her family, the Croods, lives in a dark cave following strict survival rules.
She lists other cave families who died from various causes, but says the Croods survived.
She hints their world is about to change forever.
The family performs a loud, choreographed hunting ritual for breakfast, chasing prey together.
Grug scolds Eep and others for breaking formation and leaving the cave.
The family works together to catch an egg and food, with comic mishaps between Thunk, Gran and Sandy.
They succeed in bringing food home despite chaos.
The family rushes back before nightfall, fearing darkness, while Eep resists going in and sneaks up to a ledge.
Grug scolds Eep for climbing dangerously and lectures the family about fear keeping them alive.
Grug tells the story of 'Krispy Bear,' whose curiosity got her killed, to warn Eep against curiosity.
While the family sleeps, Eep sneaks out again after hearing distant animal calls and unusual sounds.
She explores in the dark and is startled by rustling and movement in the brush.
Meanwhile Grug notices Eep is missing from the cave.
Eep meets Guy and his pet sloth Belt, who show her fire for the first time.
Guy warns her that the world is ending and offers to help her escape with him, but Eep declines and returns home.
Guy gives Eep a shell horn to call him if she needs help.
Eep returns to find her family searching for her; Grug is furious and grounds her.
Eep tries to explain about the boy she met, but the family dismisses her and are frightened of anything 'new.'
Eep shows them the horn and blows it, but Grug destroys it out of fear.
An earthquake begins, and the ground shakes violently as the family flees.
They escape as their cave and homeland are destroyed behind them.
The family finds itself in an unfamiliar jungle far below their old home.
They realize they cannot go back and must find a new cave to shelter in.
The family cautiously searches for a new cave while Grug leads with exaggerated caution.
They are chased by the Macawnivore, Chunky, and narrowly escape into a cave inside a strange creature's mouth.
They discover Chunky is afraid of the dark and laugh at him.
Birds and other creatures threaten the family, and Eep is separated in the chaos.
Eep blows the horn to call for help.
The family flees the Macawnivore until piranhakeets attack and devour a ground whale, scaring the cat away.
Guy rescues the Croods using fire, and the family reacts with fear and fascination toward him and his fire.
Grug imprisons Guy inside a hollow log to force him to guide them to safety.
The family experiences fire and cooked food for the first time, both delighted and confused.
Guy suggests they travel to a mountain that has caves, to appease Grug though he privately doubts it is safe.
The family begins a long journey together, bickering and getting used to Guy's presence, still carried in the log.
The family stops to hunt, and Grug tries to steal a bird's egg but ends up catching a scorpion instead.
Guy teaches Eep how to build a trap to catch the bird properly.
Eep and Guy work together using the trap and imitate a bird call, growing closer.
The trap fails initially, and the group ends up eating a large feast anyway.
Grug tells another cautionary story to the family about a curious tiger who dies after leaving the cave.
Guy tells his own version of the tiger story, describing 'Tomorrow,' a bright land beyond fear.
The family falls asleep, taken with the idea of Tomorrow.
The family narrowly avoids a predator and continues moving, with Guy urging more speed.
Guy accidentally reveals he can only tell stories outside the log, leading Thunk to release him by trickery.
The family struggles walking over sharp rocks and injures their feet.
Guy invents primitive shoes to help them walk safely, endearing himself to the family.
The family encounters strange fish creatures and Guy helps them safely cross the water.
The family enjoys rain and play together, with Guy telling jokes and stories.
Guy proposes the group split into pairs using shell horns to search faster; Grug refuses, fearing danger.
The group nonetheless gets briefly separated in a quicksand pit and struggles to escape together.
Thunk adopts a small creature he names Douglas as a pet.
Gran tells a story about a past love, while the family bonds and shares stories at camp.
Guy shows Eep the sky full of suns he calls Tomorrow, saying it is where they'll be safe.
Eep decides she wants to go with Guy, but Grug forbids it, causing family tension.
Grug becomes jealous of Guy's inventions and clumsily tries to create his own ideas to impress Eep.
His attempts fail comically, causing him embarrassment in front of the family.
The group reaches the mountain, but a cave collapse or eruption forces them to move on.
The family votes to go with Guy toward the sun instead of hiding in another cave, defying Grug.
Grug attacks Guy for leading his family astray, and the two fall together into a tar flow.
Believing they are doomed, Guy reveals he lost his own family to a similar tar flow long ago.
Touched by Guy's story, Grug agrees to work together with him to escape the tar.
They devise a plan requiring one of Guy's ideas to escape.
They build a puppet to lure Chunky the cat, who mistakes it for a mate and pulls them free of the tar.
Grug and Guy reunite safely with the rest of the family.
A volcanic cataclysm begins and the group flees as the ground crumbles around them.
They are halted at the edge of a great chasm as the continents drift apart.
Grug feels the sun's warmth through the smoke and realizes there may be safety on the far side.
He resolves to give up his old fears and take a chance for his family's survival.
Grug throws each family member one by one across the chasm to safety.
Before throwing Eep across, he shares his final invention, a 'hug,' and tells her he loves her.
The family lands safely on the far cliff while Grug remains behind, alone in a cave as danger closes in.
Grug hides in a cave as Chunky approaches, but the cat reveals he is scared of the dark and seeks comfort instead of attacking.
Grug hears Eep blowing her horn to mourn him and mistakes it as a call for help.
He comes up with a new idea to save himself and the animals with him.
Eep sobs, believing her father is lost, while the family listens for him across the chasm.
Grug appears riding a makeshift airship made of tar, fire, a whale ribcage and piranhakeets, flying over the chasm.
Grug is welcomed back lovingly by his family as their leader, and Eep returns his hug.
The family settles into their new life together, now with pets and looser rules.
A song plays as the family enjoys their new tropical home leading down to the seashore.
The film ends with the family thriving together in their new world.
